title: The Third Cup
logline: A grandchild remembers how their grandmother's slow coffee ceremony held a scattered family together, one cup at a time.

voice.name: Kore
voice.style: Say warmly, at a gentle natural pace:

style_block: warm hand-painted gouache illustration with visible brush strokes and paper texture, soft golden light, earthy Ethiopian palette of ochre, coffee brown, highland green and the warm white of handwoven cotton, authentic Ethiopian setting and people, main subject centered in the frame, calm composition, no text, no letters, no watermark

character.name: Emama (grandmother)
character.description: an elderly Habesha Ethiopian grandmother from the Amhara highlands, deep dark brown skin, fine Habesha facial features with high cheekbones and soft wrinkles, silver hair in thin braids under a handwoven white cotton netela with a colourful woven tibeb border of green, yellow and red patterns, wearing a white habesha kemis with matching tibeb embroidery down the front, a tiny faint traditional cross tattoo between her eyebrows, kind deep-set eyes

music.caption: instrumental, gentle Ethiopian folk underscore, soft krar plucks and warm low strings, slow and tender, sparse texture, no lead melody, nostalgic, intimate

cues.note: Music fades in softly under the dawn
Slight lift as the first cup is poured
Thins out to almost nothing: the family is apart
Theme returns warmly for the last cup, then fades under the end card

shots.reason: Establishing shot: tells the audience where and when, a highland village at dawn, before we meet anyone.
shots.image_prompt: a round Ethiopian tukul hut with a conical thatched roof and mud walls on a green Amhara highland hillside at dawn, a thin line of smoke rising through the thatch, tall eucalyptus trees, terraced teff fields and blue mountains in the morning mist
shots.motion_prompt: smoke rises slowly from the roof, mist drifts across the valley, camera slowly pushes in, fixed horizon
shots.narration_en: Every morning in my grandmother's house began the same way: with smoke, and with coffee.
shots.narration: የአያቴ ቤት ጠዋት ሁሌም በአንድ ዓይነት መንገድ ነበር የሚጀምረው፤ በጢስ እና በቡና።

shots.reason: Insert on her hands: the ritual is physical and slow, and hands carry the feeling without showing a face yet.
shots.image_prompt: extreme close-up from above of an elderly Ethiopian woman's deep dark brown weathered hands, white handwoven cotton sleeves with a colourful tibeb border, a thin silver Ethiopian cross bracelet, stirring green Ethiopian coffee beans with a metal stick in a flat iron roasting pan (menkeshkesh) over a small charcoal stove (kesel), some beans turning dark brown, wisps of smoke, no face visible
shots.motion_prompt: the hands stir the beans slowly, smoke curls upward, static camera
shots.narration_en: She roasted the green beans over the fire until they cracked and turned dark, and the whole house smelled of it.
shots.narration: ጥሬውን ቡና እሳት ላይ ትቆላዋለች፤ እስኪፈነዳና እስኪጠቁር ድረስ። ቤቱም በሙሉ በቡናው መዓዛ ይሞላል።

shots.reason: Introduces the grandmother herself: a medium shot so we see who she is and the gesture of sharing the smoke.
shots.image_prompt: inside a mud-walled Ethiopian home, the grandmother smiling and carrying a flat iron pan of freshly roasted dark coffee beans, fragrant smoke rising from them, wafting the smoke toward the viewer with her hand as Ethiopians do, a woven mesob basket and a small window with morning light behind her
shots.motion_prompt: she walks slowly forward holding the pan, smoke trails behind her, camera tracks gently
shots.narration_en: Then she carried the smoking pan to each of us. Breathe it in, she said. This is how a day should start.
shots.narration: ከዚያም የሚጤሰውን መቁያ ይዛ ወደ እያንዳንዳችን ትመጣለች። «እስቲ አሽቱት» ትላለች፣ «ቀን መጀመር ያለበት እንዲህ ነው።»

shots.reason: The first cup, abol: the pour is the most iconic image of the ceremony and starts the three-cup structure.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of a hand with deep dark brown Ethiopian skin holding a traditional black clay jebena by its handle and tilting it forward exactly like the pouring reference image, a thin stream of dark coffee falling from the long spout straight down into the opening of the cup directly below it into small white handleless sini cups painted with colourful Ethiopian patterns, exactly like the cups in the pouring reference image, arranged on a carved wooden rekebot tray, freshly cut long green grass (ketema) and yellow meskel daisies on the floor, frankincense smoke curling from a clay incense burner, plain warm mud wall in the soft-focus background, no people in the background, only one jebena in the picture, every cup is handleless
shots.motion_prompt: the coffee stream pours steadily into the cup, steam rises, incense smoke curls, camera fixed
shots.narration_en: The first cup is called abol. It is the strongest. It is for waking up.
shots.narration: የመጀመሪያው ሲኒ አቦል ይባላል። እሱ ጠንካራ ነው። ከእንቅልፍ ለመንቃት የሚጠጣ።
reference_notes: Copy the pose of the jebena, the hand and the handleless patterned cups from the pouring reference image.

shots.reason: The second cup, tona: a wide shot of family gathered, because the ceremony is about people, not coffee.
shots.image_prompt: wide shot inside a mud-walled Ethiopian home, three generations of one Habesha Ethiopian family, everyone with deep dark brown skin and Ethiopian facial features, sitting on low wooden stools around the coffee ceremony: the grandmother in her white netela at the center pouring from the jebena, a mother with braided shuruba hair in a white habesha kemis, a father wrapped in a white gabi, a dark-skinned Ethiopian boy and girl with curly black hair laughing, a woven basket of kolo roasted barley and a bowl of popcorn, frankincense smoke, green grass on the floor
shots.motion_prompt: people talk and gesture gently, incense smoke drifts, slow camera pan
shots.narration_en: The second cup, tona, was for talking. This is where all the family stories came out.
shots.narration: ሁለተኛው ሲኒ ቶና ለጨዋታ ነው። የቤተሰቡ ታሪኮች በሙሉ የሚወጡት እሱ ላይ ነበር።
reference_notes: The jebena she pours from must look exactly like the clay pot in the second reference image.

shots.reason: Close-up of her face for the emotional peak: the blessing and her rule that nobody leaves early.
shots.image_prompt: close-up portrait of the grandmother smiling with closed eyes, holding a small white sini coffee cup near her face with both hands, steam rising, warm golden light on her cheek, the tibeb border of her netela framing her face
shots.motion_prompt: she slowly opens her eyes and smiles, steam rises from the cup, very slow push in
shots.narration_en: The third cup is baraka, the blessing. Nobody leaves before the third cup, she always told us.
shots.narration: ሦስተኛው ሲኒ በረካ ነው፤ ምርቃቱ። «ከበረካ በፊት ማንም አይነሳም» ትለን ነበር ሁሌም።

shots.reason: The turn: the same room, empty and dim. Absence shows how the family has scattered.
shots.image_prompt: the same mud-walled Ethiopian room now empty and quiet in dim blue evening light, the traditional Ethiopian jebena from the jebena reference image: a dark brown-black clay coffee pot with a round spherical body resting on a small woven ring stand, a tall narrow neck topped with a small clay lid, a spout rising diagonally from the lower body, and a handle curving from the neck down to the shoulder standing alone on a carved wooden rekebot tray, three empty small white sini cups, dried yellowed grass on the floor, a cold clay incense burner, a woven mesob basket in the corner
shots.motion_prompt: dust floats in a thin beam of light, nothing else moves, camera slowly pulls back
shots.narration_en: Now our family lives in four cities and two countries. We rarely sit together for three cups.
shots.narration: አሁን ቤተሰባችን በአራት ከተሞች እና በሁለት አገር ነው የሚኖረው። አብረን ተቀምጠን ሦስቱን ሲኒ የምንጠጣው አልፎ አልፎ ነው።
reference_notes: The jebena must look exactly like the clay pot in the jebena reference image.

shots.reason: Resolution: the grandchild continues the ritual in a modern apartment, closing the motif of the third cup.
shots.image_prompt: the traditional Ethiopian jebena from the jebena reference image: a dark brown-black clay coffee pot with a round spherical body resting on a small woven ring stand, a tall narrow neck topped with a small clay lid, a spout rising diagonally from the lower body, and a handle curving from the neck down to the shoulder, standing upright on the windowsill of a small modern apartment at dawn with steam rising from its spout, a young Ethiopian woman's dark brown hand holding a small white handleless sini cup of dark coffee beside it, a few blades of green grass and a tiny incense burner on the sill, the Addis Ababa skyline with high-rise buildings and the Entoto hills outside the window, the same warm golden light, no face visible, only one jebena in the picture
shots.motion_prompt: steam rises from the jebena and the cup, the hand slowly raises the cup, morning light grows, static camera
shots.narration_en: But when I make coffee, I still roast it the slow way. And I always wait for the third cup.
shots.narration: እኔ ግን ቡና ሳፈላ አሁንም ቀስ ብዬ ነው የምቆላው። ሦስተኛውንም ሲኒ ሁልጊዜ እጠብቃለሁ።
reference_notes: The jebena must look exactly like the clay pot in the jebena reference image.
